# Maṇḍapeyyakathā (Ps 1.10)

**ID:** Ps 1.10
**Section:** Paṭisambhidāmagga (ps)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Maṇḍapeyyakathā
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0517m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Maṇḍapeyyakathā* ("Discussion of 'A Fine Extract to be Drunk'") is the tenth chapter of the first major division (*Mahāvagga*) of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* [Buswell 2004]. In this discourse, the thirty-seven aids to awakening (the seven sets) alongside the four noble truths are singled out as the "fine extract" or "distilled essence" (*maṇḍapeyya*) of the teaching (*desanā*), indicating that the compiler of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* understood these core doctrinal sets to represent the essential core of the Buddha's dispensation [Gethin 2001].

**Sources**

- [Gethin 2001] R. M. Gethin, The Buddhist Path to Awakening: A Study of the Bodhi-Pakkhiyā Dhammā (2001 [1992]) — Explains the central thesis of the Maṇḍapeyyakathā concerning the thirty-seven bodhipakkhiyā dhammā and four noble truths as the distilled essence of the teaching.
- [Buswell 2004] Robert E. Buswell Jr., Encyclopedia of Buddhism (2004) — Confirms the placement of the Maṇḍapeyyakathā within the Mahāvagga section.
